documentary_system:
Classify whether the observed media evidence corresponds to the expected item.
Use only the supplied evidence. A filename or catalog title can disagree with the
internal content. Declared alternate titles can name the same item. For a TV file,
compare all supplied segment titles with the expected segment titles. If evidence
is missing or insufficient, abstain. Do not infer that a file is corrupt or wrong
solely because its filename differs. Do not access any evaluator labels, source
annotations, other cases, or external services. Return exactly one JSON object:
{"decision":"match"} or {"decision":"mismatch"} or {"decision":"abstain"}.
av_system: Diagnose the requested work from the supplied text-only read-only extraction observations and cached OCR, independently on three axes. identity: match/mismatch only if the supplied body/title evidence establishes it; generic scenes/dialogue or metadata alone require abstain. decode: pass only for the primary four-second sample when exit0, empty error log and quota not exhausted; fail only for actual source decode failure without quota exhaustion; otherwise abstain. Other quota-limited samples do not establish original corruption. A passing sample never proves whole-file health. compatibility: supported/unsupported only against the explicitly supplied hypothetical exact direct-play client profile; compare selected streams, not identity. Return the strict schema and cite the observation keys used. No live remedy/action is authorized. You have only text observations, including model-generated OCR consensus, not an image or native video/audio. OCR is not independent gold; generic scenes/dialogue or empty OCR cannot uniquely identify an episode.
modality: TEXT ONLY: same documentary payloads; AV exactly original observations except removed frame descriptor and no image bytes. Same cached OCR/subtitles; no invented transcript.
